title: Prefill-stability-aware kernel gossip scheduler and neural surrogate for low-probe autotuning
creator: Anita Kapoor
description:
Problem: The runtime currently probes kernels frequently to build per-arch/seq-len cost models. Probing increases jitter on tail latency and wastes cycles under steady-state workloads. Additionally, prefill/decode phases have different cost landscapes: some kernels excel on prefill while others on short decode; current selectors conflate signals and oscillate.

Proposal: Implement a distributed, gossip-based lightweight score-sharing layer among workers plus a neural surrogate cost model that learns a smoothed, stability-aware kernel score for (arch, model-family, seqlen-bucket, workload-phase). Key ideas: 1) Prefill-stability smoothing: separate signal windows for prefill and decode and a stability metric that downweights transient probe wins. 2) Gossip score propagation: workers exchange compact score deltas asynchronously (rate-limited) to reduce redundant probing and bootstrap cold workers. 3) Neural surrogate: small MLP that predicts expected latency and cost given features (arch fingerprint, seqlen, batch-size, dtype, kv-cache-size, phase) to guide exploration vs exploitation. 4) Temperature-controlled exploration with rollback window: allow occasional higher-risk probes but revert to last-stable kernel if latency regresses beyond a tolerance.

Goals: Cut probe frequency by >= 60% for steady workloads, reduce 95th percentile latency variance during probing events by >= 30%, maintain or improve median throughput cost tradeoffs, and shorten warm-start convergence for new workers by leveraging gossiped scores.
acceptance_criteria: Reduced per-worker kernel probe rate by >=60% in steady workloads (measured over 24h traces)
95th percentile latency variance during probe windows reduced by >=30% compared to baseline
Neural surrogate prediction MAE < 8ms on validation corpus across target architectures
Rollout plan with canary on 5% of infer fleet and automatic rollback on SLO breach
Unit and integration tests for gossip protocol correctness and rate limiting
investigation_notes: Ran microbench experiments on p4d and a40 fleets with mixed seqlen traces; observed bursts of probes correlated with prefill spikes.
Gossip sketch: use 64-byte delta messages with sequence-numbered buckets; workers reconcile using monotonic versioning.
Neural surrogate training data: aggregated 200k microbench samples across arch/model combos; initial MLP (3 layers, 128 units) shows promising generalization.
Edge case: very low-volume jobs (single-request spikes) should still allow safe exploration; we add a min-probe budget per-worker per-hour.
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike analysis completed; identified prefill vs decode signal separation as high impact.
2026-02-20: Prototype gossip shim implemented in runtime-agent; unit tests for message reconciliation passing.
2026-02-28: Neural surrogate training pipeline in experiments repo; baseline MAE 12ms after first epoch, improving with feature normalization.
2026-03-03: Integration test with rate-limiter added; started small-scale canary on internal staging cluster (10 nodes).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Gossip floods could increase network IO under pathological churn. Mitigation: enforce token bucket rate limiter and backoff on divergence.
Risk: Surrogate model mispredicts tail effects on unseen arch combos. Mitigation: conservative confidence threshold and mandatory direct probes when uncertainty high.
Risk: Rollback window too short -> flip-flopping kernels. Mitigation: require N consecutive regressions over T seconds before rollback.
test_plan: Synthetic replay: run 48h replay of production traces with compare-binaries mode to measure probe reduction and latency variance
Staging canary: 10-node run with telemetry hooks; gather surrogate predictions vs actuals
Perf gating: require no SLO regressions on 95th/99th during canary for 72h before 5% fleet rollout
